newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM says holding line on economic reform.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM says holding line on economic reform.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Saturday he was pursuing economic reforms launched by the previous Congress government and dismissed reports of growing strains with his reluctant ally.

"There is no question of any digression from economic and industrial policies of the previous government," Deve Gowda told reporters at a reception he hosted for prominent Moslems to mark the fasting month of Ramadan.

Deve Gowda said he and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram are leaving on January 31 for Davos in Switzerland where they are expected to defend India's economic policy at the World Economic Forum meeting.
"The talk about strains with (the Congress) stems from media disinformation," he said.

Deve Gowda was speaking a day after he was sharply criticised by the Congress Parliamentary Party whose 137 deputies in the Lok Sabha (lower house of parliament) are shoring up the ten-month old United Front government.

The United Front took power last June after the Congress suffered a humiliating defeat in general elections. There has been widespread uncertainty over economic liberalisation, which Congress launched in 1991, under Deve Gowda's leadership.

"Serious concern was expressed at the hike in prices, about the drift in the economic situation and its management," Congress spokesman Vithal Gadgil told reporters after a meeting of the party's senior parliamentarians on Friday.
"Foreign investments are going down, industrial production is slowing down and there is a sharp fall in the rate of exports," Gadgil said.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram appeared to corroborate that gloomy analysis on Saturday when he said plans to sell about $1.4 billion worth of shares in state-owned firms were unlikely to be achieved by the end of the current fiscal year.
"The present process of disinvestment is nonsensical," Omkar Goswami, professor at New Delhi's Indian Statistical Institute told a conference on divestment of shares in state-owned firms.
The government has set a target of raising 50 billion rupees ($1.4 billion) in 1996/97 (April-March) from divestment, or the sale of partial stakes in state-controlled firms.
Deve Gowda's United Front alliance on Friday discussed its strategy for the budget session of parliament which is expected to start on February 20.
Analysts said the uneasy alliance between the United Front and Congress could hit a flashpoint in debate over the budget for fiscal 1997/98 ending March 31.

Deve Gowda, with fewer than 200 supporters in the 545-seat Lok Sabha (lower house of parliament), needs the support of the Congress deputies to beat off a relentless challenge from the main opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
